basis: Parasitic infection; urinary and intestinal injury varies by species and clinical expression. Significant hepatic fibrosis affects a minority across this umbrella.
Defining skeletal and nail abnormalities; despite frequent developmental-delay annotations, the definition describes resolving motor delay without established lasting neurologic injury.
Skeletal dysplasia; structural cleft lip/palate reported in 1/2 patients supports gastrointestinal involvement. Reflux and recurrent otitis are separate conditions.
Thiamine-deficiency metabolic encephalopathy causes structural brain injury; ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic injury rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Familial dilated cardiomyopathy; hepatomegaly and elevated transaminases accompanying severe heart failure do not establish direct hepatic involvement.
Deficient gonadotropin signaling causes hypogonadism; anosmia and intellectual disability are occasional, below 30%.
Defining neural tube defects, oral clefts/omphalocele and diaphragmatic skeletal-muscle defects; renal and cardiac anomalies occur in only 5-29%.
Glycosylation disorder; developmental regression, seizures and brain atrophy occur in 1/1 patient, as do structural limb joint contractures. Single-patient evidence.
Inherited retinal degeneration with night blindness, visual field loss and reduced visual acuity in 3/3 patients.
Named syndrome defines abnormal hair growth, skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability; hirsutism alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Usually benign amino-acid metabolic defect; causality of reported intellectual disability/seizures is unestablished despite frequent HPO annotations. Stones are occasional.
Congenital spinal dysraphism with a defining midline cutaneous malformation connected to the spinal cord by a fibroneural stalk.
Severe Hallermann-Streiff-like disorder supports ocular and craniofacial skeletal malformations; family-specific evidence for additional organ involvement is unavailable.
Tubular aggregates, muscle-fiber atrophy and weakness define skeletal myopathy; ophthalmoplegia occurs in 2/11 and respiratory insufficiency in 5-29%.
Radial/skeletal defects, ocular motility abnormalities and congenital hearing loss define the syndrome; thrombocytopenia occurs in 13/21 patients (~62%).
Purine metabolic defect; neurologic dysfunction affects most patients (~80%, complete/intermediate deficiency). Urate stones and gout are separately diagnosed diseases.
Ocular glaucoma-suspect/borderline condition; established optic nerve damage is not required for this eye-specific diagnosis.
Named congenital association combines a diaphragmatic skeletal-muscle defect, exomphalos with displaced abdominal viscera and corpus callosum agenesis.
Defined by failure of pulmonary gas exchange; hypoxia and hypercarbia do not by themselves establish additional organ injury.
Tick-borne infectious illness; the transient erythema migrans-like rash does not establish lasting skin injury.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with characteristic ST elevation and risk of ventricular fibrillation; no other organ disease is established.
Cerebral motor disorder; fixed joint contractures with structural shortening develop in well over 30% during the typical course of severe quadriplegic cerebral palsy.
Infectious abscess directly destroys lung parenchyma; no additional organ involvement is required or commonly intrinsic.
Reported inherited lipid-storage disorder; intellectual disability and splenic abnormalities lack frequency and functional-damage evidence sufficient for additional labels.
Hamartoma arising in breast tissue, which is outside the 13 axes.
